title: Make every path agree on which car a plate is

blocks.text: A city sells residents' parking permits, one per car. Residents type their plate the way it is printed, so the same car arrives as `KL-482-T`, `kl 482 t` or `KL482T`: capitals or not, with spaces, dashes or neither, it is one car. Street cameras report plates as they read them, in the same variety.

Last month registration was fixed to treat those spellings as one car. Since then, two complaints have come in: a resident who holds a permit was fined by a camera, and a permit was moved onto a car that already held one, so it now has two.

Finish the `TODO` in `src/main/java/practice/Permits.java`, `plateKey(...)`, and change anything else in the file you need to. When you're done, registration, transfer and the camera's check agree on which car a plate is, however each was written, and on any server. About six lines in total.

cases.says: with plates written the same way everywhere, permits are registered, seen by the camera and transferred, and a car never holds two
the camera's check recognises a car whose permit was bought with the plate written another way
a transfer is refused when the target car already holds a permit under another spelling of its plate
a permit transferred from a plate written with spaces leaves that car without a permit
a plate typed in lower case with an i matches the camera's reading under a Turkish default locale

origin.section: One Method Decides When Two Names Are the Same, and Every Path Calls It

concepts: A key that folds case uses Locale.ROOT, so it is the same on a server whose default locale is Turkish.
The single representation of an equality rule is one method whose result keys the data, so every path, including one added later, goes through it.
